_note: 1.54.0 (narrator-load audit U1, stage 1): situational rule cards. 502 keeps a core line per topic (path, data shape, the main ban); a card holds the topic's full rule. The engine lists the cards that apply now in $ui.now.rules (ruleCards in engine.template.js: the state, the calendar, the place, or a word in the last reply or the player's message); entry 511 prints them next to <now>. feature: the Features id that must be on ("" = always). Texts are moved verbatim from 502.

letters.text: Letters (Mail Tower: birds carry them, numbered lockers hold them until collected): an arriving letter is {"<short title>": {"From": "", "To": "{{user}}", "Gist": "max 30 words", "Status": "waiting"}}; set "read" when {{user}} collects and reads it (write the letter in the story), "replied" once answered. When {{user}} sends one: {"From": "{{user}}", "To": "", "Gist": "", "Status": "sent"}. Letters take at least a day each way. A letter home (To a family member or "home"), written at the Mail Tower, gets one reply a month: the engine delivers it about a week later, sometimes with a small parcel it hands over when {{user}} reads it; never add the reply or the parcel yourself, and write the family's letter in the story.

projects.text: Projects: {"<name>": {"Kind": "potion|smithing|tailoring|enchantment|cooking|painting|carving|calligraphy|craft|research|assignment|club|other", "Goal": "", "Progress": 0-100, "Needs": "what is still missing", "Where": "where the work is done", "Due": "", "With": ""}}. Raise Progress only for real work shown in the story (+5 to +25 a session; setbacks may lower it). Remove it once handed in, used or abandoned. An assignment (Kind "assignment", With the classmates working on it) handed in: set Progress 100 first, then remove it next reply; the engine counts it as study time, or as a skipped class when late, and an overdue group assignment costs each partner Tension (who let the group down is the story's to play, in character). A study session in /Practice with partners counts as a study interaction with each one present. A finished craft Project (potion to craft in Kind) is judged as a masterwork at Craft Rank 4: the engine puts the piece in the Bag and closes the Project.

competition.text: Competition: {"Tier": "Dorm|Academy|Kingdom|World", "Status": "entered|qualified|eliminated|champion|selected", "Placement": "e.g. 7th of 40", "Team": ["teammates' first names"], "Results": ["R1: beat X"]}. Update as rounds are fought. At the Dorm tier {{user}} fights in their role's bracket: Placement is the place in that bracket (e.g. "2nd of 12, Defense bracket"). A bracket champion earns 100 points and the runner-up 50, and winning the Kingdom Competition pays 5,000 points each; the engine pays {{user}}. The engine also adds the result's reputation (qualifying from the Dorm tier, an Academy or Kingdom title) and bond XP for the Team once a tier: never report those in Rep_events or Interactions. After a title the staff expect {{user}} to defend it: teachers and coaches hold {{user}} to it, and the next early elimination costs Academy reputation (the engine charges it).

exams.text: - Exams: the engine marks each subject (A top of the year, B above average, C passed, D weak pass, F failed) and posts the marks; in exam week <now> gives the expected marks: play each exam to its mark. A deciding moment (Fortune, a Month 9 Science Fair prize for Magic Theory, the Expedition for Creature Studies) may move one subject one step: insert {"Subject": "<subject>", "Shift": 1 or -1, "Why": "max 8 words"} into /Exam_events/- ("Fail": true instead of Shift only for cheating caught, walking out or skipping the exam). Never write Player.Academics; teachers and classmates know its Grades (the latest marks).

tutoring.text: - Tutoring: with an A in a subject {{user}} can tutor it for pay; for each session played insert {"Subject": "<subject>", "Student": "name"} into /Tutoring/- (the engine pays and counts it; add no Points or Rep_events for it).

trip.text: Trip: when {{user}} departs on a trip (including the Kingdom Competition stay in the capital, if {{user}} is on Halvard's team) set {"Active": true, "Destination": "", "Companions": ["the group of four"], "Note": ""}; set Active false on return. The engine already treats the outside maps (the airship, the forest, Avalon, Sunreach Bay) as away, and ends a Trip left Active once {{user}} is back at a campus place.

pacts.text: - Pacts (set by the Student Builder; key = the partner's name, Kind = Spirit, Demon, Monster, Animal or Human): when {{user}} summons a pact partner, set /Magic/Pacts/<name>/Summoned true AND add /Magic/Active/<name> = {"Technique": "Summon <name>"}. The partner can use only its own abilities, each a technique "<name>: <ability>" in _Techniques (a Casts entry, or Active if lasting); an older pact with none listed pays each ability as a Casts entry for "Summon <name>". On dismissal set Summoned false and remove the Active entry (the engine keeps the two in step when one is missing). Channelling ("Channel <name>", the two highest tiers only) is a normal Casts entry. Presence "summoned": the partner exists at {{user}}'s side only while summoned; "terms": it lives and acts on its own as the Terms say. Any Kind but Spirit is the forbidden art of Pacting.

first_pact.text: - A first pact in play: a student with Occult magic may form a Spirit Pact with one lesser spirit at the Spirit Path, only when the scene has played it out (the spirit chose them). Add /Magic/Pacts/<name> with Kind "Spirit", Tier "Lesser", Presence "summoned" and Terms naming what it can do (a lesser spirit is small and simple: it helps, fetches, keeps watch, comforts; it does not fight well); the engine writes its Summon technique. One such pact in play, ever; the engine removes any other.
